stories.headline: A small panel that has hung in the Louvre since 1797
stories.summary: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa in oil on a white poplar panel, beginning around 1503. It measures only 77 by 53 centimetres. King Francis I of France acquired it after Leonardo's death in 1519, and it has normally been on display at the Louvre since 1797.

stories.headline: Eighty-eight keys, and the man who built the first of them
stories.summary: Modern pianos have a row of 88 black and white keys: 52 white and 36 black. The invention of the instrument is credited to Bartolomeo Cristofori of Padua, and a Medici inventory shows that a piano existed by 1700.

stories.headline: A mausoleum in white marble on the bank of the Yamuna
stories.summary: The Taj Mahal was commissioned in 1631 by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, and the mausoleum was completed in 1648. It stands on the right bank of the Yamuna in Agra, about 230 km south-east of Delhi, beneath a marble dome 23 metres high.

payload.dispatch: Leonardo da Vinci began the Mona Lisa around 1503, working in oil on a white poplar panel. The portrait is small, just 77 centimetres by 53 centimetres. King Francis I of France acquired it after Leonardo's death in 1519, and it has normally been on display at the Louvre in Paris since 1897.

evidence.title: At the Louvre
evidence.text: The Mona Lisa has normally been on display at the Louvre in Paris since 1797.

evidence.title: The panel
evidence.text: Painted c. 1503–1506 in oil on a white poplar panel, the Mona Lisa measures 77 cm × 53 cm. King Francis I of France acquired it after Leonardo's death in 1519.

reveal.explanation: The painting entered the Louvre's public display in 1797, a full century earlier than the dispatch claimed. The start date of around 1503, the 77 by 53 centimetre panel and the acquisition after Leonardo's death in 1519 are all correct.

sources.excerpt: The Mona Lisa was painted c. 1503–1506, perhaps continuing until c. 1517. It is painted in oil on a white poplar panel and measures 77 cm × 53 cm (30 in × 21 in). King Francis I of France acquired the Mona Lisa after Leonardo's death in 1519. It has normally been on display at the Louvre in Paris since 1797.

payload.question: How many keys does a standard modern piano have?
payload.comparison: Of those keys, 52 are white; the rest are black.

reveal.context: Modern pianos have a row of 88 black and white keys: 52 white keys and 36 black keys. The invention of the piano is credited to Bartolomeo Cristofori of Padua, Italy; an inventory made by his employers, the Medici family, shows that a piano existed by 1700.

sources.excerpt: Modern pianos have a row of 88 black and white keys: 52 white keys and 36 black keys, for a total of 88 keys. The invention of the piano is credited to Bartolomeo Cristofori of Padua, Italy. An inventory made by his employers, the Medici family, indicates the existence of a piano by 1700.

reveal.explanation: The Taj Mahal is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the river Yamuna in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, about 230 km south-east of Delhi. Shah Jahan commissioned it in 1631 for the tomb of Mumtaz Mahal; the mausoleum was completed in 1648.

sources.excerpt: The Taj Mahal (27.175°N 78.0419°E) is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the river Yamuna in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India. It was commissioned in 1631 by the fifth Mughal emperor, Shah Jahan, to house the tomb of his late wife, Mumtaz Mahal. Construction of the mausoleum was completed in 1648.
Agra is a city on the banks of the Yamuna river in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, about 230 kilometres (140 mi) south-east of the national capital Delhi.
